data_output.description: data.py load() continues returning raw rows as (date, user_id, video_id, label). encode() builds user_id and video_id vocabularies from the training split only, derives weekday directly from each row date using a deterministic seven-category mapping, and returns each split as (features, labels, users), where features is an int32 matrix with columns [encoded_user_id, encoded_video_id, encoded_weekday], labels is float32, and users preserves original validation user IDs and row order. Unknown user, video, or weekday values use reserved training-derived indices. No future-event aggregation, validation labels, or evaluator metrics are used.

model_input.description: model.py Model.logits(), step(), predict(), state(), and load_state() accept the encoded three-column feature matrix [user_id, video_id, weekday]. The logit is bias + user effect + video effect + user-video embedding dot product + weekday embedding dot video embedding dot product. Training remains pointwise binary cross-entropy with the existing optimizer and L2 behavior. predict() returns one finite float score per input row in identical order. train.py must emit predictions_valid.npz containing exactly two arrays, row_ids=np.arange(len(validation_rows), dtype=int64) and scores, with no ground-truth array; row_ids and scores must follow canonical validation row order.
